GRANT AGREEMENT

Between the Everleigh Family Foundation and Cedar Hollow Community Health Collaborative

Grant No. EFF-2026-0217

This Grant Agreement is made as of April 6, 2026, between the Everleigh Family Foundation, a Michigan nonprofit corporation (the "Foundation"), and Cedar Hollow Community Health Collaborative, a Michigan nonprofit corporation exempt from federal income tax under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code (the "Grantee").

1. GRANT AMOUNT AND PERIOD

1.1 Award. The Foundation awards the Grantee a grant in the amount of $425,000 (the "Grant"), payable in accordance with the schedule in Section 1.3.

1.2 Grant Period. The period of performance runs from May 1, 2026 through April 30, 2028 (the "Grant Period"). Costs incurred before the start or after the end of the Grant Period are not allowable and may not be charged against the Grant.

1.3 Payment Schedule. The Foundation shall disburse the Grant in four installments: $150,000 within fifteen (15) days after the Foundation receives this Agreement signed by the Grantee; $125,000 on or about November 1, 2026, following acceptance of the first interim report; $100,000 on or about May 1, 2027, following acceptance of the second interim report; and the remaining $50,000 within thirty (30) days after the Foundation accepts the final narrative and financial reports. The Foundation may withhold any installment if a required report is overdue or if the Grantee is in breach of this Agreement.

2. RESTRICTED PURPOSE AND BUDGET

2.1 Restricted Purpose. The Grant funds shall be used solely for the mobile dental clinic program described in the Grantee's proposal dated February 12, 2026, and in accordance with the approved budget attached as Exhibit A. The Grant is a restricted use grant. No portion of the Grant may be used for any other program, for endowment, for capital construction, or to cover a deficit from a prior fiscal year.

2.2 Budget Deviation. The Grantee may reallocate up to ten percent (10%) of any approved budget line to another approved line without notice. Any budget revision that exceeds ten percent (10%) of a line, that changes the scope of the program, or that adds a new budget category requires the Foundation's prior written approval, which will not be unreasonably withheld. A request for a budget modification shall be submitted at least thirty (30) days before the change takes effect.

2.3 Indirect Costs. The Grantee may charge indirect costs against the Grant at a rate not exceeding fifteen percent (15%) of modified total direct costs.

3. REPORTING

3.1 Narrative Reports. The Grantee shall submit interim narrative reports describing progress against the program objectives and the outcome measures in Exhibit B. Interim reports are due no later than October 15, 2026, and April 15, 2027. The final narrative report is due within sixty (60) days after the end of the Grant Period.

3.2 Financial Reports. The Grantee shall submit a financial report with each narrative report, showing expenditures by budget line against the approved budget, and shall submit a final financial report within sixty (60) days after the end of the Grant Period.

3.3 Prompt Notice. The Grantee shall notify the Foundation in writing within thirty (30) days of any change in the Grantee's executive leadership, any loss or threatened loss of its exemption under Section 501(c)(3), any material change in the program, and any event that makes it unlikely the program objectives will be met within the Grant Period.

4. UNEXPENDED FUNDS AND REPAYMENT

4.1 Unexpended Funds. Any unexpended funds remaining at the end of the Grant Period shall be returned to the Foundation within sixty (60) days after the end of the Grant Period, unless the Foundation approves a carry-forward in writing before that date.

4.2 Repayment. The Grantee shall repay to the Foundation, on demand, any portion of the Grant that (a) is used for a purpose other than the restricted purpose stated in Section 2.1, (b) is not expended within the Grant Period and is not approved for carry-forward, or (c) is determined by the Foundation, after notice to the Grantee and a reasonable opportunity to respond, to have been expended in violation of this Agreement. The Foundation may also suspend or terminate further disbursements and require the return of previously disbursed funds if the Grantee loses its exemption under Section 501(c)(3).

5. USE RESTRICTIONS

5.1 Lobbying and Political Activity. No part of the Grant shall be used to carry on propaganda or otherwise to attempt to influence legislation within the meaning of Section 4945(d)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code, to influence the outcome of any specific public election or to carry on any voter registration drive within the meaning of Section 4945(d)(2), or to support or oppose any candidate for public office or any political campaign or political action committee. The Grantee shall not use Grant funds for lobbying as that term is defined in Section 4911(d).

5.2 Non-Charitable Purposes. No part of the Grant shall be used for any purpose other than one specified in Section 170(c)(2)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code, and no part shall be used to make a grant to an individual for travel, study, or similar purposes.

5.3 Anti-Terrorism. The Grantee represents that it does not and will not knowingly provide material support to any individual or entity on the Specially Designated Nationals list maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control.

6. RECORDS, AUDIT, AND ACCESS

6.1 Records. The Grantee shall maintain books and records adequate to show the receipt and expenditure of the Grant separately from its other funds, in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.

6.2 Retention. The Grantee shall retain all records relating to the Grant for at least four years after the date the final financial report is submitted, and longer if any audit, claim, or litigation relating to the Grant is then pending.

6.3 Audit and Access. The Foundation and its representatives may inspect the Grantee's records relating to the Grant, and may visit the program site, on reasonable notice during normal business hours. If the Grantee expends $750,000 or more in federal awards in a fiscal year, it shall provide the Foundation with a copy of its Single Audit report within thirty (30) days after issuance.

7. GENERAL

7.1 Publicity. The Grantee may acknowledge the Foundation's support in program materials. Neither party shall use the other's name or logo in a manner suggesting an endorsement of an unrelated product or position without prior written consent.

7.2 Independent Contractor. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency, or employment relationship. The Grantee is solely responsible for the conduct of the program and for its employees, volunteers, and subcontractors.

7.3 No Assignment; Subawards. The Grantee shall not assign this Agreement or subaward any portion of the Grant without the Foundation's prior written consent. Any approved subrecipient is bound by Sections 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 of this Agreement, and the Grantee remains responsible for the subrecipient's compliance.

7.4 Termination. The Foundation may terminate this Agreement and cease further disbursements upon written notice if the Grantee breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after notice. Upon termination, the Grantee shall submit a final narrative and financial report within sixty (60) days and return all unexpended funds. Sections 4, 6, and 7.5 survive termination of this Agreement.

7.5 Governing Law; Forum. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Michigan. Any action arising out of this Agreement shall be brought in the state or federal courts located in Washtenaw County, Michigan.

7.6 Entire Agreement; Amendment. This Agreement, together with Exhibit A and Exhibit B, is the entire agreement of the parties concerning the Grant and may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties.

The parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.

EVERLEIGH FAMILY FOUNDATION
